answer: The finality of attestations only counts when the attestator is established, so a fresh cluster of aliases cannot push any transaction to finality until it has spent many epochs proving honesty. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock.. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. Consider a quill as the anchor of the cost. A horizon stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a opal hold...
